## TC-07: Session-level data augmentation

| | | | |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Software component:** | Session-level data augmentation | | |
| **Reference:** | `src/ingestion/augment.py`, `src/ingestion/source.py`, `scripts/train_models.py`, `src/spu/splits.py`; `tests/test_augment.py` `TestAugmentation` | | |
| **Test Case ID:** | TC-07 | **QA Test Engineer:** | Abi |
| **Test case Version:** | 3 | **Reviewed By:** | - |
| **Test Date:** | 2026-11-23 | **Use Case Reference(s):** | - |
| **Revision History:** | v1 2026-11-15 (a497de6); v2 2026-11-15 (be0a468); v3 2026-11-16 (d3ab703) | | |
| **Objective:** | Check that augmentation parameters are fixed per (session, copy) and reproducible, that the same transform is applied to every frame of a copy, that the augmented frame source keeps the original timestamps, and that augmented rows never enter a test fold. | | |
| **Product/Ver/Module:** | FYP-1 attention pipeline, commit `9245f93`. Ingestion and training: makes augmented copies of whole sessions (flip, colour shift, noise, masks) that are read on the fly and used only to train models and tune the tracker. | | |
| **Environment:** | Windows 10 (10.0.19045); conda environment fyp-local: Python 3.13.18, NumPy 2.5.5, SciPy 1.18.1, scikit-learn 1.9.1, pandas 2.3.3, OpenCV 4.11.0, PyTorch 2.9.0+cu126. CPU only; no GPU, dataset or model weights needed unless stated. Run from the repository root: python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . | | |
| **Assumptions:** | The augmentation settings come from configs/deliverable3.json (hue_deg 3 at the time of writing). Small synthetic ZIP files of 4 PNG frames (64 x 48 random noise, named images/10_00_0<i>_000000.png) stand in for DIPSER camera ZIPs. A tiny DataFrame stands in for the training table. | | |
| **Pre-Requisite:** | Run from the repository root; configs/deliverable3.json and the results files read by configs/derived.py must exist (the config is loaded at import). OpenCV, pandas and PyTorch installed. Test ZIPs are written only to temporary directories. | | |

| Step No. | Execution description | Procedure result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `test_hflip_mirrors_boxes`: Call hflip_boxes on box [[10, 5, 30, 20]] with frame width 100, then flip the result again. | The flipped box is [[70, 5, 90, 20]]. Flipping twice returns the original box. (Passed) |
| 2 | `test_parameters_are_fixed_per_session_and_copy`: Call sample_augmentation for session 'group_01/experiment_01/context_cam_01' copy 1 twice, for the same session copy 2, and for 'group_02/experiment_01/context_cam_01' copy 1. | The two calls with the same session and copy give equal parameters. A different copy number, and a different session, each give different parameters. (Passed) |
| 3 | `test_hue_shift_stays_small`: Sample parameters for 50 sessions ('s0' to 's49') and copies 1 and 2, and collect hue_deg. | Every \|hue_deg\| is at most the configured hue_deg, and the configured hue_deg is at most 5 degrees. (Passed) |
| 4 | `test_tag_ignores_copy_count`: Compute aug_tag for copy 1 with the config's settings at copies = 1 and at copies = 3, and with hue_deg changed to 4. | The tag is the same for copies = 1 and copies = 3. Changing hue_deg to 4 gives a different tag. (Passed) |
| 5 | `test_same_transform_on_every_frame_noise_aside`: Take the sampled parameters for session 's' copy 1, with noise 0 and hflip True. Apply augment_frame to two identical 8 x 8 frames of value 40, as frame indices 0 and 1. | The two output frames are identical: the flip, colour shift and masks do not change from frame to frame. (Passed) |
| 6 | `test_source_is_a_dataset_with_the_original_timestamps`: Write a 4-frame ZIP. Build an AugmentedZipFrameSource with only hflip on (noise 0, no masks, neutral colour: brightness 0, contrast 1, saturation 1, hue 0, gamma 1) and a plain ZipFrameSource on the same ZIP. | The augmented source is a torch Dataset with length 4. Its timestamps equal the plain source's. Item 2's image equals the plain frame 2 flipped horizontally. Iterating it yields frame indices [0, 1, 2, 3]. (Passed) |
| 7 | `test_a_copy_is_the_same_video_every_time_it_is_read`: Write a 4-frame ZIP. Read all frames through AugmentedZipFrameSource with copy 1 parameters for 'group_01/experiment_01/context_cam_01' and noise 0.3, then read them again with freshly sampled copy 1 parameters and noise 0.3. Read frame 0 with copy 2 parameters and noise 0.3. | Every frame of the two copy 1 reads is identical, noise included. Frame 0 of copy 2 differs from frame 0 of copy 1. (Passed) |
| 8 | `test_augmented_rows_never_reach_a_test_fold`: Build a table of 6 rows: groups [g1, g1, g2, g2, g1, g2], aug flags [False, False, False, False, True, True]. Iterate heldout_splits from scripts/train_models.py. | In every fold, no test row is augmented; the training rows include augmented rows (copies of the other group); and no training row belongs to the held-out group. (Passed) |

**Comments:** Augmented copies are never written to disk. test_a_copy_is_the_same_video_every_time_it_is_read checks that seeding alone makes every read of a copy identical.

| **Product/Ver/Module:** | FYP-1 attention pipeline, commit `9245f93`. Feature pass, first step: turns the frame-pass tracker output into tracklets and removes short or broken pieces before windowing. | | |
| **Environment:** | Windows 10 (10.0.19045); conda environment fyp-local: Python 3.13.18, NumPy 2.5.5, SciPy 1.18.1, scikit-learn 1.9.1, pandas 2.3.3, OpenCV 4.11.0, PyTorch 2.9.0+cu126. | **Assumptions:** | A synthetic tracker output stands in for real tracks: one track (TID 7) with a fixed box [0, 0, 10, 10], confidence 0.9 and a per-frame signal 'sig' equal to the frame time. Gaps are counted in existing frames that lack the track, converted to seconds with the given fps. | | |
| **Pre-Requisite:** | None beyond the Python environment. | | |

| Step No. | Execution description | Procedure result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `test_split_where_tracker_lost_the_track`: Frames exist every 0.2 s from 0 to 3.8 s (5 fps). The track is present at t = 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 2.4, 2.6, so it is absent from 8 existing frames (1.6 s). Build the tracklet, then call filter_visible with fps 5, max_gap_s 1.0 and min_visible_s 0.0, then again with min_visible_s 0.7. | The built tracklet's 'sig' signal equals the input times [0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 2.4, 2.6]. With min_visible_s 0.0 the tracklet is split into two pieces of 4 and 2 observations. With min_visible_s 0.7 only the 4-observation piece (0.8 s visible) is kept; the 2-observation piece (0.4 s) is dropped. (Passed) |
| 2 | `test_camera_frame_drop_is_not_a_gap`: Frame times are [0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 3.6, 3.8]: the camera dropped 3 s of frames, but the track is present in every frame that exists.
